About

behind the interface.

How does an API handle a request? How should data move through an application? What changes when a system gets bigger? Those are the kinds of questions that keep me interested in computer science.

I work mostly with Java, Python, and C, and I’ve been building web applications with React and Node.js. Projects and hackathons have given me room to try things, get stuck, debug, and learn how to work with other people.

At UCF, I’m building on that experience through coursework in algorithms, object-oriented programming, discrete mathematics, computer logic, and cybersecurity.

Featured work

GitHub ↗
NUTRITION / FULL STACK

NutriPlanner

Nutrition tracking, from a C engine to a web application.

A nutrition application with a C engine for calorie targets, macro calculations, and meal logging. The web application includes integrations for USDA food search, AI-assisted planning, and Supabase authentication and sync. API-dependent features are currently inactive while API funding is pending.

Challenge Keeping nutrition calculations separate from the interface while bringing food data, user input, and AI guidance into one application.

  • C
  • Node.js / Express
  • REST APIs
  • Supabase
  • OpenRouter
GitHub repo ↗Live demo ↗

Demo status: interface available; AI/API features are currently inactive pending API funding.

Project notes

How it is structured

The C core handles nutrition calculations and dynamic meal logging. The web layer uses an Express API deployed as serverless functions, with separate services for food search, AI, and account sync.

What I learned

Defining clear API boundaries, working with explicit memory management, and debugging data flows across different parts of an application.

Validation in the repository

The core includes unit tests through CTest, a CLI demonstration, and an automated GitHub Actions build and test workflow.

AI / DATA PROCESSING

GatorPlanner

Making financial data easier to explore.

A stock analysis application that brings financial data and AI-generated insights into one interface. I worked on Gemini integration, asynchronous market-data pipelines, and backend processing in Python.

Challenge Combining external market data and AI-generated output in a backend workflow that a React interface can use.

  • TypeScript
  • React
  • Node.js
  • Python
  • Gemini API
Live demo ↗Repository not listed
Project notes

The work

Connected market-data processing with an AI service and a user-facing application. The project gave me practice thinking through asynchronous workflows and how information moves between services.

What I took away

A better understanding of backend data processing, API integration, and presenting complex information in a usable interface.
